articles.title: Process Automation for Swiss SMEs: A Control, Exception, and Recovery System
articles.excerpt: Process automation fails in small companies for a surprisingly ordinary reason: the team automates a visible task before it understands the decision, data, exception, and recovery path around that tas…
articles.body: Process automation fails in small companies for a surprisingly ordinary reason: the team automates a visible task before it understands the decision, data, exception, and recovery path around that task. The demo works. The first clean cases pass. Then a supplier changes a PDF, a customer replies from a different address, an API times out, or an employee corrects a record after the workflow has already propagated it. The automation has not removed work; it has converted familiar work into opaque operational debt. This guide adapts the practical tool and use-case overview in IAPME Suisse's process automation guide for Swiss SMEs .

articles.title: Decision Brain: giving AI the why behind the work, with FalkorDB
articles.excerpt: Decision Brain: giving AI the why behind the work, with FalkorDB I built Decision Brain around one problem: giving AI real memory of why things are the way they are. Imagine taking every change in the…
articles.body: Decision Brain: giving AI the why behind the work, with FalkorDB I built Decision Brain around one problem: giving AI real memory of why things are the way they are. Imagine taking every change in the documents a business runs on — Word files, spreadsheets, policies, code — and mapping them into one memory layer in a graph, where every change is connected to the decision behind it, the evidence, and the people who know it. For this hackathon (Graph Hacks, FalkorDB × WeMakeDevs) I started where that information is richest: code repositories. Every change is already recorded, and good teams write their decisions down. And code has a real problem. Code shows what a program does, but not why .

articles.title: My self-hosted ad blocker poisoned Apple's push servers and killed iMessage
articles.excerpt: I run AdGuard Home in Docker on a spare Linux box at home. Every device on my network gets it as DNS through DHCP, so the laptops, the phones, the TV, all of them resolve through one container I contr…
articles.body: I run AdGuard Home in Docker on a spare Linux box at home. Every device on my network gets it as DNS through DHCP, so the laptops, the phones, the TV, all of them resolve through one container I control. For a few weeks it looked like the cleanest thing in my homelab. 18 filter lists, 85 user rules papering over the false positives, ads gone everywhere including the TV. Then iMessage stopped sending and receiving on my Mac. The symptom was confusing. Restart the Mac, messages arrive fine for about 30 minutes, then everything queues and never delivers. The BlueBubbles API returned status 200, message sent, every single time. chat.db told the truth, error 4, is_delivered 0.

articles.body: Companion Podcast The Hidden Cost of AI Hype: Why Your Setup Matters More Than the Model (A FinOps Post-Mortem) For the past five years, I’ve been deep in the trenches of AI development—configuring local networks, deploying containers, writing calculation contracts, and wiring up cloud environments. Like many of you, I spent years chasing the benchmark dragon, constantly migrating my workflow to whoever released the "smartest" model that week. But as we close out 2026, I’ve had a harsh realization. The intelligence of the AI is no longer the bottleneck. The real bottleneck is how we structure our toolbelt. We are bleeding money, compute, and time because we are using the wrong architectures for the wrong stages of our development cycles.

articles.title: Your Discovery Example Is a Promise — We Replayed 1,602 of Ours to Check
articles.excerpt: A 402 response is not just a price. In the extensions.bazaar block it can also carry an input example and an output example — a sample request and a sample answer. Directory crawlers index them, and a…
articles.body: A 402 response is not just a price. In the extensions.bazaar block it can also carry an input example and an output example — a sample request and a sample answer. Directory crawlers index them, and agents use them to decide whether an endpoint does what they need before they pay. That makes an example a claim. If the sample answer disagrees with what the handler actually returns, the agent has three bad options: conclude the endpoint is broken, conclude the platform is lying, or spend money to find out. None of those are good, and all of them are avoidable if the example is true. We replayed ours to see how many were.

articles.excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, the Antares rocket now built by Northrop Grumman Space Systems returned to flight to come back from a catastrophic explosion. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

articles.excerpt: John Stewart goes rogue in Sector 2814 and embraces fear hopefully leading into season 2
articles.body: HBO and HBO Max's " Lanterns " served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were. While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling. After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
